newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels kill 21 soldiers in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels kill 21 soldiers in ambush.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels killed 21 Sri Lankan soldiers when they ambushed an army patrol in eastern Trincomalee district on Sunday, military officials said.
They said an army road clearing patrol was attacked by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels at Pulmoddai, 17.6 km (11 miles) north of Trincomalee early on Sunday.
"Reinforcements had been rushed to quell the attack and fighting is now over," said a military official in Trincomalee, 240 km (150 miles) east of the capital Colombo.
"We lost 21 soldiers," he added. The official said it was not immediately known whether the LTTE had suffered any casualties.
A military spokesman in Colombo confirmed the incident but said he was still waiting for details.
An LTTE spokesman was not immediately available for comment on Sunday's attack.
The LTTE, who are fighting for an independent homeland in Sri Lanka's north and east, said they killed 23 soldiers in another ambush in the eastern Batticaloa district last week.

They said in a statement from London on Sunday that the rebels had intercepted an army patrol near Valaichchenai, near Batticaloa, 220 km (130 miles) east of Colombo and lost two of their fighters in the gunbattle that lasted some 15 minutes.
But military officials put the army casualty toll at 12.

The statement said the rebels had also killed four soldiers in a separate attack on Friday near the main Sri Lanka army camp in Batticaloa. There was no immediate confirmation available from the military.
The goverment says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the number is higher.
